description: We are young innovators passionate about climate science, technology and environmental solutions. Our project, El Niño Uganda, uses NASA Earth observation data to help communities understand rainfall patterns and climate risks. Our skills and interests include software development, GIS, climate research and data analysis. We welcome team members skilled in programming, UI/UX design, meteorology and community engagement who want to make climate information accessible to everyone.
summary:
El Niño Uganda is an interactive climate information platform developed to help Ugandans understand how El Niño influences rainfall patterns and what changing weather conditions could mean for their communities.

The platform brings NASA Earth observation data into an interactive map of Uganda, allowing users to select their location and explore rainfall conditions, climate risks and practical guidance. Rather than presenting complicated scientific information, the system explains environmental conditions in simple language that people can understand and relate to their everyday lives.

The project focuses on farmers, students, local communities and decision-makers who need accessible climate information to support planning and preparedness.

By combining satellite observations, geographical visualisation and location-specific explanations, El Niño Uganda makes climate science more accessible. Our aim is to help communities understand rainfall variability, recognise potential risks and make better-informed decisions in response to changing environmental conditions.
details:
El Niño Uganda

Understanding Climate, Preparing Communities

The Problem

Rainfall plays an important role in Uganda's agriculture, water supply, infrastructure and everyday life. When rainfall patterns change, communities can experience flooding, water shortages, crop losses and disruption of economic activities.

El Niño is one of the climate phenomena that can influence seasonal rainfall in East Africa. However, its effects are not uniform across Uganda, and understanding its possible influence requires reliable climate information.

Although satellite observations and climate datasets are available, much of this information remains difficult for people without scientific training to interpret.

We developed El Niño Uganda to address this gap.

Our Solution

El Niño Uganda is a web-based platform that makes climate information easier to explore and understand.

The platform uses an interactive map of Uganda to connect environmental observations with individual locations. Users select an area and receive a simple explanation of relevant rainfall conditions, possible risks and practical measures to consider.

Instead of expecting people to interpret technical datasets, the platform communicates climate information through accessible language and visualisation.

How It Works

1. Select a location

Users explore the interactive map and select an area of Uganda.

2. Explore climate information

The platform presents rainfall-related information associated with the selected location, drawing on NASA Earth observation resources.

3. Understand local conditions

The information is translated into a short explanation describing rainfall patterns and possible implications for the area.

4. View risk indicators

Simple categories help communicate whether rainfall-related conditions are higher, normal or lower relative to the relevant comparison.

5. Explore practical guidance

Users receive general recommendations for preparing for rainfall variability and associated environmental risks.

Technology and Development

The project was designed using modern web development technologies:

  • Next.js and React for the web application.
  • TypeScript for application development.
  • Tailwind CSS for responsive interface design.
  • Interactive geographical visualisation for exploring Uganda.
  • NASA Earth observation resources for environmental information.

The interface prioritises readability, straightforward navigation and accessibility across different screen sizes.

What Makes the Project Innovative?

El Niño Uganda is built around a simple question: How can people understand climate information without needing to become climate scientists?

The innovation lies in connecting scientific environmental observations with explanations that are relevant to specific locations.

Rather than displaying satellite data alone, the platform provides an experience that helps people explore what the information may mean in their communities.

It brings together geographical interaction, environmental data, simple risk communication and practical guidance in one accessible platform.

Who Benefits?

Farmers: Better understanding of rainfall variability and potential agricultural risks.

Students and educators: An accessible tool for learning about El Niño and climate science.

Communities: Greater awareness of changing rainfall conditions and possible impacts.

Local decision-makers: An additional source of accessible environmental information for public awareness and planning.

Scientific Considerations

El Niño does not produce the same rainfall conditions everywhere. Its influence depends on the season, location and interaction with other climate systems.

The platform therefore treats satellite observations as scientific information for understanding climate conditions, not as guaranteed predictions of future weather.

Future Development

We intend to expand the platform with additional environmental indicators, improved local-language accessibility, historical rainfall comparisons and broader geographical coverage.

Conclusion

El Niño Uganda was developed to make climate information easier to access and understand.

By bringing NASA Earth observation data into an interactive platform focused on Uganda, we aim to help people connect scientific information with the environmental challenges affecting their communities.
